Western disturbances give about 10-15 cm of winter precipitation to north-western India, useful for rabi crops. Mango showers are pre-monsoon convectional (not temperate frontal) rain, Mawsynram is on the windward side (orographic rain), and Ruyli in Jaisalmer is India's driest place, not a wet Western Ghats station (those are Agumbe and Hulikal).

Aandhi is the summer dust-laden storm of the dry north-western plains. Mango showers are pre-monsoon convectional showers, not Himalayan snowfall; the loo is a hot, dry wind of the northern plains, not an Assam storm; and cherry (coffee) blossoms are showers linked to coffee flowering in Karnataka, not a hot, dry wind.

Tauktae (2021) was an Arabian Sea cyclone that hit Gujarat and its offshore infrastructure. Biparjoy was an Arabian Sea cyclone that hit Gujarat (Chennai floods were from Michaung), Michaung was a Bay of Bengal cyclone, and Fengal (Bay of Bengal, 2024) struck the Tamil Nadu-Puducherry coast; Mozambique was hit by Idai.
